corrections.why: The 1948 article says the wood tower extends 16 feet above the ground. 18.3 m is 60 feet, the standard steel tower the article says this one was not built as.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register (2014) and the state list both mark the tower as standing, so the record's standing status holds. Neither source describes its current condition.

sources.title: Chimney Top
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (easternuslookouts.weebly.com), quoting the Kingsport Times-News of August 29, 1948

notes_for_editor: The 1948 build date rests on a newspaper report reproduced on Forest Lookouts; the register gives no build date, only a September 5, 1948 date under the name that it does not explain. Height: the record's 18.3 m equals the 60-foot standard steel tower that the article contrasts with this one; the article gives 16 feet above ground, so a correction is proposed, not applied. Disagreements left open: county (register says Hawkins; article says on the Greene and Hawkins line); elevation (article 3,018 ft ground; register 2,960 ft; state list shows a different figure, 3118 ft, not used). The register and state list both misspell or vary the agency name in places; the record's typo is the one corrected. Not verified: current condition, public access, climbing status, staffing after 1948, and any fire it watched.
